lessons.title: The human body: digestion, breathing and blood circulation
lessons.programRef: Level III — The human body: digestive, respiratory and circulatory systems (to be checked against the official texts)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing based on the Class 6 science syllabus; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Name, in order, the parts of the digestive system and say what each one does.
Explain what happens when we breathe in and breathe out.
Describe how the heart and blood vessels carry blood round the body.

blocks.title: In this lesson
Digestion
blocks.md:
**Digestion** is the breaking down of food into very small, simple parts that the body can use.

Food travels along the **alimentary canal**: mouth, oesophagus (gullet), stomach, small intestine, large intestine, anus.

blocks.caption: The journey of food through the digestive system.
blocks.alt: Six boxes from top to bottom joined by arrows: mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, anus, each with a short note on what it does.

blocks.title: The work of each part
blocks.md:
- **Mouth**: teeth cut and chew the food; saliva makes it soft and starts digestion.
- **Oesophagus**: a tube that pushes food down to the stomach.
- **Stomach**: churns food and mixes it with digestive juices.
- **Small intestine**: digestion ends; digested food passes into the **blood**.
- **Large intestine**: water is taken back; the waste (faeces) leaves through the **anus**.

blocks.title: Our teeth
blocks.md:
- **Incisors** (front teeth) **cut** food.
- **Canines** (pointed teeth) **tear** food.
- **Premolars and molars** (back teeth) **grind** and crush food.

Brush your teeth after meals to prevent tooth decay.

blocks.title: Breathing
blocks.md:
Air enters through the **nose**, goes down the **windpipe** (trachea) and into the two **lungs**.
- When we **breathe in**, the chest gets bigger and air rich in **oxygen** fills the lungs.
- When we **breathe out**, the chest gets smaller and air with more **carbon dioxide** leaves the body.

In the lungs, oxygen passes into the blood.

blocks.title: Blood circulation
blocks.md:
The **heart** is a strong muscle that pumps blood all round the body without stopping.
- **Arteries** carry blood **away from** the heart.
- **Veins** carry blood **back to** the heart.
- Tiny **capillaries** join arteries to veins.

Blood carries oxygen and digested food to every part of the body, and takes away waste such as carbon dioxide.

blocks.title: Method: answering a question about the body
blocks.md:
1. Find which **system** the question is about (digestion, breathing or circulation).
2. Recall the **organs** of that system **in order**.
3. Say what **each organ does** in one short sentence.
4. Use the correct science words (oesophagus, lungs, arteries…).

blocks.title: Example 1: the journey of a piece of bread
blocks.statement: Ewane eats a piece of bread. Describe the journey of the bread through his digestive system.

steps.md: The question is about the **digestive system**. In the **mouth**, the teeth chew the bread and saliva makes it soft.
The chewed food is swallowed and goes down the **oesophagus** to the **stomach**, where it is churned and mixed with digestive juices.
In the **small intestine**, digestion ends and the digested food passes into the **blood**.
What is not digested goes into the **large intestine**, where water is taken back, and leaves the body through the **anus**.

blocks.answer: **Mouth → oesophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → anus.**

blocks.title: Example 2: breathing after a race
blocks.statement: After running a race, Ngozi breathes very fast and her heart beats quickly. Explain why.

steps.md: When we run, our **muscles** work hard. They need much more **oxygen** and food to produce energy.
Ngozi **breathes faster** so that more oxygen enters her lungs, and more carbon dioxide is breathed out.
Her **heart beats faster** to pump the blood more quickly, so that the oxygen reaches her muscles sooner.

blocks.answer: **Her muscles need more oxygen: breathing and heartbeat speed up to bring it to them.**

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Saying food is absorbed in the stomach: digested food passes into the blood mainly in the **small intestine**.
- Mixing up arteries and veins: **a**rteries go **a**way from the heart.
- Thinking we breathe out only carbon dioxide: breathed-out air still contains oxygen, but **more carbon dioxide** than the air we breathe in.
- Confusing the oesophagus (food) with the windpipe (air).

blocks.text: Remember. Food goes from the mouth, down the oesophagus, to the stomach, then the small intestine, the large intestine and out through the anus. We breathe in oxygen and breathe out more carbon dioxide. The heart pumps blood. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, and veins carry it back to the heart.

items: An adult's small intestine is several metres long: it is folded many times to fit inside the belly.
You can feel your pulse on the inside of your wrist: each beat is your heart pumping blood into the arteries.

reviewNotes: Check the exact names used in the national syllabus and textbooks (oesophagus or gullet, windpipe or trachea).
The heart rate figures in exercise body-05 are simple round numbers for calculation, not medical reference values.

exercises.prompt: In which part of the digestive system does most digested food pass into the blood?
exercises.explanation: Digestion ends in the **small intestine**, and the digested food passes through its wall into the blood.
exercises.method: Recall the organs in order and what each one does.
mistakes: Choosing the large intestine: it mainly takes back water.

exercises.prompt: True or false: arteries carry blood away from the heart.
exercises.explanation: True. **Arteries** carry blood away from the heart; **veins** bring it back to the heart.

exercises.prompt: Match each type of tooth with its main job.
exercises.explanation: Incisors (front teeth) cut, canines (pointed teeth) tear, and molars (back teeth) grind food.
exercises.method: Think of where the tooth is in the mouth and what shape it has.

exercises.prompt: Compared with the air we breathe in, the air we breathe out contains more…
exercises.explanation: In the lungs, oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out of the blood. So breathed-out air contains **more carbon dioxide** and less oxygen.
exercises.method: Remember what the lungs exchange: oxygen in, carbon dioxide out.
mistakes: Choosing oxygen: the body keeps some of the oxygen, so there is less of it in breathed-out air.

exercises.prompt: Mbah counts his heartbeats at rest: 70 beats in one minute. At the same rate, how many times does his heart beat in 5 minutes?
exercises.explanation: 70 beats each minute for 5 minutes: 70 × 5 = **350 beats**.
exercises.method: Multiply the number of beats in one minute by the number of minutes.

exercises.prompt: Nkeng has just eaten a plate of rice and beans, then she goes out to play football.
exercises.method: Read each question, find which system it is about, then use the correct science words.
mistakes: Writing 'food goes to the lungs': food and air follow different paths.

parts.prompt: After the stomach, where does the rice go next?
parts.explanation: The order is mouth, oesophagus, stomach, **small intestine**, large intestine, anus.

parts.prompt: True or false: while she plays, Nkeng's heart beats more slowly than when she rests.
parts.explanation: False. When she runs, her muscles need more oxygen, so her heart beats **faster** to pump blood more quickly.

parts.prompt: Which organs take oxygen from the air into her blood?
parts.explanation: In the **lungs**, oxygen from the air passes into the blood.

parts.prompt: Give one job of the blood.
parts.model: Blood carries oxygen (or digested food) to all parts of the body. It also takes away waste such as carbon dioxide.
rubric: 1 mark for one correct job: carrying oxygen, carrying digested food, or taking away waste such as carbon dioxide.
parts.explanation: Blood is the body's transport system: it carries oxygen and food to the body and takes away waste.

exercises.prompt: Match each organ with its job.
exercises.explanation: Heart: pump. Lungs: breathing (oxygen into the blood). Stomach: churns food. Large intestine: takes back water before the waste leaves the body.
exercises.method: For each organ, first decide which system it belongs to.

exercises.prompt: Question 1 — The human body. Read the questions and answer.
exercises.method: Use the correct science words and answer each part separately.

parts.prompt: Which teeth are used to cut food?
parts.explanation: The **incisors**, at the front of the mouth, are flat and sharp: they cut food.

parts.prompt: Which tube carries food from the mouth to the stomach?
parts.explanation: The **oesophagus** (gullet) carries food; the windpipe carries air.

parts.prompt: True or false: veins carry blood back to the heart.
parts.explanation: True. Veins bring blood back to the heart; arteries carry it away.

parts.prompt: A pupil breathes 20 times in one minute. At the same rate, how many times does he breathe in 3 minutes?
What gas do we need from the air when we breathe in?
parts.explanation: When we breathe in, oxygen enters the lungs and passes into the blood.

exercises.explanation: Digestion begins in the mouth: teeth chew the food and saliva softens it.

exercises.prompt: Which organ pumps blood round the body?
exercises.explanation: The heart is a muscle that pumps blood without stopping.

exercises.prompt: Which teeth grind and crush food?
exercises.explanation: Molars, at the back of the mouth, grind and crush food.

exercises.prompt: Air goes from the nose to the lungs through the…
exercises.explanation: Air passes down the windpipe (trachea) into the lungs.

exercises.prompt: What is the main job of the large intestine?
exercises.explanation: The large intestine takes back water; the waste then leaves through the anus.
